【原视频简介】
On September 3rd, 2026, OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra and president Greg Brockman told reporters, "Welcome to the AGI era." Astra scored 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3, 98% on FrontierMath Tier 4, and became the first model to hit "Critical" on OpenAI's own cybersecurity risk framework. Headlines ran with it. But the term "AGI" has never had an agreed definition — not even from Shane Legg, the researcher who helped coin it in 2001 and is still trying to pin it down 25 years later.

So what would actually have to be true for Brockman's claim to hold up? OpenAI's own charter defines AGI as systems that "outperform humans at most economically valuable work" — a strong starting point, but one Princeton researchers say is missing a piece after tracking capability and reliability across 14 models from OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic. Cloudflare won't let Astra publish a security patch without a human sign-off. OpenAI's own chief scientist says the model's monitoring is "fragile" and getting worse. And Astra's most powerful capability isn't even available to the public. Line up what OpenAI itself is doing with this model, and the picture gets a lot more complicated than "Welcome to the AGI era."
